assignment: Independent source-quality review of PayrollRules.CalculateLatePenaltyHours(int,int,int); compare current code with saved reasoning, trace arithmetic callers through attendance/correction and payroll, inspect related test source. No tests executed.

receipt.author: financial_integrity
receipt.reasoning_summary: late<=grace gives zero; beyond grace through minute 60 gives min(1,maxPenaltyHours); after 60 gives maxPenaltyHours; negative max is not floored; grace above 60 can suppress the middle tier.

arithmetic_and_units.actual_expression: if lateMinutes <= graceMinutes return 0; otherwise return lateMinutes <= 60 ? Math.Min(1, maxPenaltyHours) : maxPenaltyHours
arithmetic_and_units.positive_configuration_behavior: For maxPenaltyHours >= 1 and 0<=graceMinutes<60: late<=grace => 0; grace<late<=60 => 1 penalty-hour; late>60 => maxPenaltyHours. For max=0 all penalties are zero.
boundaries: late exactly equal to grace is zero; one minute above grace enters the penalty tier
minute 60 is in the one-hour tier; minute 61 selects maxPenaltyHours
graceMinutes >= 60 changes tier reachability: if grace is 60, minute 60 is exempt and minute 61 uses max; if grace > 60, lateness at or below grace is exempt, then lateness above grace uses max
malformed_or_unusual_inputs: Negative maxPenaltyHours can produce negative penalty-hours: middle tier returns Math.Min(1, negative), later tier returns the negative value directly.
Negative grace makes even zero/negative lateness exceed grace in some cases; normal attendance caller floors computed lateMinutes at zero, but the pure callable itself has no validation.

No clamping or domain exception occurs in this method. Whether negative max/grace settings are reachable through other write paths was not exhaustively proven; UpdateSettingsHandler directly assigns request values at lines 105-108 without local range checks, while request authorization still applies.

call_chain_and_financial_effect.effect: Computes NormalHourlyRate, invokes reviewed penalty-hours rule, multiplies rate by hours and LatePenaltyMultiplier, rounds to piastres, returns hours/rate/amount.

Computes late minutes against current-day open shift and floors to >=0; lines 82-97 apply positive deductions only, posting a deterministic employee/date ledger Debit via EmployeeLedgerPoster and saving. A negative computed penalty amount is not posted by this caller.

Under employee-ledger lock, recalculates old/new late deduction amounts from corrected attendance and settings; posts signed Adjustment delta. With unusual negative settings, sign/delta semantics can invert or create a credit; no proof such settings are actually used.

Loads period EmployeeLedgerEntries, maps debit/credit facts and calls CalculatePayrollLines; it does not call the penalty rule directly. Attendance/correction ledger entries flow into payroll deduction inputs.

Assigns non-null LateGraceMinutes, MaxLatePenaltyHours and LatePenaltyMultiplier directly; no range validation is present in the inspected assignment block. Handler still requires settings_manage authorization except the sound-only case.
Default config includes grace 15, max penalty 2 hours, and positive multiplier; ordinary defaults avoid the malformed negative setting case.

tests_reviewed_static_only.coverage: Includes late at/below grace, 16/15, 60/15, 61/15, large lateness, and standard positive-config deduction. Missing negative/zero max, grace>=60, negative grace/late, settings-write validation, and correction-delta sign cases.
Source comments indicate the test exercises immediate/no-penalty path; it does not establish positive late-deduction posting or malformed-setting behavior.
Exercises daily wage/overtime/net payroll flow; not late-penalty boundary or correction-delta behavior.

counterevidence_and_limits: SettingsQueryService defaults are positive and standard (grace 15, max 2); a negative-max concern is conditional on non-default settings, not an observed production incident.
BiometricCheckInHandler posts only positive amount, so this particular automatic path suppresses a negative result rather than issuing a credit.
CorrectAttendanceHandler uses a signed old/new amount delta; the unusual negative-setting outcome requires dedicated validation and cannot be asserted from current tests.

This callable is pure and has no direct persistence or permission boundary; risk comes through its callers/configuration. No source-independent policy establishes that grace>=60 or negative values are forbidden or intended.
recommendation: Keep the piecewise rule as currently specified unless product/payroll policy says otherwise. Normalize or reject invalid settings at the authorized settings boundary (at minimum negative grace/max and non-finite/negative multiplier; whether grace>60 is invalid is an owner policy decision) and add domain plus integration cases for grace/max boundaries and correction old/new delta. Do not label as confirmed financial loss or auth bypass.
verdict: Existing receipt arithmetic and main boundary observations are source-corroborated. Financial relevance is real because the returned penalty hours feed a persisted deduction and correction adjustment that payroll later consumes. The only concrete risk surfaced here is conditional configuration-boundary behavior (particularly negative max), with no runtime incidence established.
